near.why: "NEAR Protocol is the blockchain for AI" and "a sharded blockchain architecture" -- it ships the chain agents settle on; manual names NEAR under the chain facet.

bittensor.why: CG label DePIN plus "an open-source protocol that powers a decentralized, blockchain-based machine learning network" where "machine learning models train collaboratively and are rewarded in TAO" -- what is sold is intelligence, not machine time.

internet-computer.why: "Sovereign frontier cloud for AI" that runs "entire software systems end-to-end on the network" for "AI agents and agentic organizations"; it ships consensus, so chain dominates the cloud pitch. Manual names Internet Computer under chain.

render-token.why: "a leading decentralized GPU compute platform for applications ranging from 3D rendering to machine learning and generative AI" -- metered GPU time. Read rather than ruled because its NFT and Metaverse labels would misfire.

grass.why: CG label DePIN; homepage blurb "Grass turns the unused part of your internet into rewards" is thin, but the manual names Grass explicitly under the data facet (crawling / data supply for AI).

the-graph.why: "The Graph is an indexing protocol and global API for organizing blockchain data" -- the resource layer the stack reads from. Read, not ruled: its Analytics label would misfire on an indexing protocol.

theta-token.why: CG label DePIN; "the edge network provides vast amounts of GPU compute power for AI, video, rendering and other tasks" -- metered throughput. Manual names Theta under compute despite the Theta Blockchain.

akash-network.why: CG label DePIN; "an open-source, decentralized, marketplace for cloud computing" where "users can lease out their unused computing capacities" -- rented machine time.

arweave.why: CG labels DePIN and Storage; "a new data storage blockchain protocol ... that creates truly permanent data storage" -- persistent storage, the manual's data facet.

permacast.why: Only "The AI-Powered Permanent Media Network." -- permanent media hosting reads as a storage layer rather than a producer of media; coded with Arweave as sibling. Thin one-line blurb, hence low.

golem.why: CG label DePIN; "an open-source, decentralized computing platform ... to provide computing power to the AI industry. A peer-to-peer marketplace for distributed computing resources."

chutes.why: "Deploy, run and scale any AI model in seconds. Try directly through our platform, or use our easy-to-use API" -- what is sold is a model's answer through an API, not a rented pod, so model rather than compute. Bittensor subnet facet follows what the subnet does.

aethir.why: CG label DePIN; "Enterprise-grade AI-focused GPU-as-a-service provider ... decentralized cloud computing infrastructure allows GPU providers (containers) to meet Enterprise clients".

sentient.why: "an open-source intelligence network" whose GRID is "a decentralized fabric of specialized agents, models, datasets, tools, and compute ... working together as one to deliver high-quality results" -- the output is the answer. Manual names Sentient under model.

celium.why: "Rent H100, B200, RTX 4090 and more GPU pods at marketplace prices, billed per second" -- metered hardware time, so compute even though it is a Bittensor subnet.

pearl-2.why: "Pearl network -- a Proof-of-Useful-Work L1 protocol, where mining is produced natively from AI computations" -- it ships consensus, so chain dominates the AI-compute side.

arkham.why: CG label Analytics; "Arkham Intel provides traders with advanced analytics to inform their trading and risk management" plus "AI-powered market analysis" -- the product shipped is information. Not also defai: Arkham Exchange is a human CLOB venue, not agent execution.

kaito.why: CG label Analytics; "$KAITO is the native token and the fundamental building block of the AI-powered InfoFi network" -- market intelligence, the product is information.

targon.why: "Targon is a decentalized, frontier AI lab" -- a network whose output is a model; manual names Targon under the model facet. One-line blurb, hence medium.

aioz-network.why: CG label DePIN; "AIOZ rewards you for sharing your computational resources for storing, transcoding, and streaming digital media content and powering decentralized AI computation" -- metered throughput.

livepeer.why: CG label DePIN; "a live video streaming network protocol" where "nodes who contribute processing and bandwidth earn ETH" -- rented capacity and bandwidth.

story-2.why: "a purpose-built layer 1 blockchain designed to facilitate registration of intellectual property (IP) of AI-related data" -- it ships a chain, and the manual's chain test is that the project ships one (cf. ZIGChain). Borderline against the data facet, hence medium.

qubic-network.why: "Qubic is a decentralised Layer 1 network" whose "Useful Proof of Work ... channels computational power toward AI training"; manual names Qubic under chain.

zignaly.why: "ZIGChain (ZIG) is a purpose-built Layer 1 blockchain for wealth generation" -- it ships a chain; manual names ZIGChain under the chain facet, so the RWA wording does not move it to rwa.

diem.why: "Each Diem token represents $1 per day of Venice API capacity" and "DIEM transforms AI compute from a service you rent into an onchain asset you own" -- metered inference capacity. Tokenizing it is packaging, not a second function.

io.why: CG label DePIN; "the world's largest decentralized computing network that allows machine learning engineers to access scalable distributed clusters" -- rented cluster time.

score.why: Description is a repository summary only -- "Subnet 44 on Bittensor - Validator and Miner base code"; the manual names Score under the model facet. github-sourced blurb, hence low.

acurast.why: CG label DePIN; "this verifiable, scalable, and confidential compute network enables developers to run secure applications" and "already powers ... LLM inference" -- metered smartphone compute. Verifiability is a property of the capacity sold, not a second trust product.

subsquid.why: "an innovative decentralized data lake and query engine ... optimized for blockchain indexing" -- the manual's data facet; read rather than ruled because the Analytics label would misfire on an indexing network.

efficientfrontier.why: "Revolutionizing Crypto Trading with Decentralized AI" -- an AI-driven trading application whose shipped product is signals, coded analytics on the manual's Rift AI / Polymtrade pair; nothing in the blurb says it executes, so not defai.

templar.why: "Templar is a decentralized AI training network. Market-driven incentives for loss reduction, enabling permissionless distributed deep learning" -- the output is a set of weights.

ocean-protocol.why: CG labels DePIN and Storage; "an ecosystem for sharing data and associated services" that "helps to unlock data, particularly for AI" -- a data marketplace, the manual's data facet.
